Class 5 · Chapter 5 of 10

Angles, symmetry, perimeter and area

Name the measurement needed before using shape facts.

  1. See it
  2. Try it
  3. Practise it
  4. Print it
  5. Check it

This chapter works best after Tenths, hundredths and decimal calculations. You can still look around, or jump to the check.

By the end I can…

  • I can find a perimeter or area.
  • I can use angle facts.
  • I can complete symmetry or fold a cube net.

1 See it

Screen 1 of 5

Angles on a line

A straight line makes an angle of 180 degrees.

If one angle is 76 degrees, the other is 180 − 76.

The other angle is 104 degrees.

Screen 2 of 5

Perimeter and a missing side

A rectangle has a perimeter of 42 m and one side of 9 m.

Two sides of 9 m use 18 m. 42 − 18 = 24 m for the other two sides.

Each of those sides is 12 m.

Screen 3 of 5

Area of a step shape

Split the shape into rectangles, or take a corner away.

A 6 by 6 square with a 2 by 2 corner removed has 36 − 4 = 32 squares.

Its area is 32 square units.

Screen 4 of 5

Symmetry

Fold along the mirror line. Matching squares land on top of each other.

Count how many squares are on each side.

The mirror makes a twin for every shaded square.

Screen 5 of 5

Fold a cube net

A cube net has 6 squares joined along edges.

When it folds, squares in a row of 3 make faces that face each other.

The first and third squares in a row end up opposite.

Words to know
angle
The turn between two lines that meet. We measure it in degrees.
perimeter
The distance all the way round a shape.
area
The space inside a shape, in square units.
line of symmetry
A mirror line that makes two matching halves.

For parents

What your child learns

A composite shape can be split into rectangles or made by taking a part away. Angles on a straight line add to 180 degrees. For a rectangle, half the perimeter is the length plus the width.

A common slip

Children often add instead of subtracting a removed corner. Find the whole rectangle, then take away the missing part. Check angle sums.

5-minute home activity: Step shapes

  1. Draw a 7 by 5 rectangle on grid paper.
  2. Cut a 1 by 2 corner away.
  3. Count the squares left.
  4. Draw a straight line with 3 angles and find the missing one.
